title: Screen overlay
description: The ground a whole screen stands on: the shell's needle gradient with a photograph from its CDN laid over it in luminosity blend at a whisper of opacity, and the photograph's credit pinned to the bottom-right corner. Children are the screen's own layout; the root is an inline-size container.

anatomy.description: Root div with data-slot="screen-overlay": the needle-400 to needle-700 gradient, min-height 100svh, isolated, and an inline-size container named screen-overlay. Accepts div props; `image` swaps the photograph and its credit together.

A ::before layer reading --image-url (set by the component from `image.url`): cover, luminosity blend, 7.5% opacity, pointer-events none. It lends texture and light and takes the ground's green, so no colour outside the palette enters.
A p with a link to the photograph's page, absolute at the bottom-right: text-2xs, needle-100; bloom-200 on hover, the sidebar's outline step (--nav-outline) on focus.

usage: Wrap a screen's layout in it when the screen stands directly on the ground, outside the sidebar shell: the login screen is the reference consumer.

The photograph is a url() to its CDN, so nothing ships in the bundle; pass `image` ({ url, creditHref, caption }) to change it and the credit changes with it. Keep the Unsplash (or equivalent) licence satisfied through the caption.
Keep the blend and the low opacity: luminosity takes the ground's green so the palette stays the only colour source; higher opacity washes out bark-50 copy on the ground.
Query the ground's width from a child's CSS with an unnamed @container (or the name screen-overlay), not a media query, so the layout answers to the space the screen has.
The credit is the last element in DOM order, so it is the last Tab stop of the screen; a consumer that wants its form focused first sets autoFocus on its first field.
Route code never styles the ground; a screen that needs a different ground is a variant here, not a rule in a route module.
